questions: Does the string S need to be reduced to an empty string using only the deletion of the exact substring "()" (i.e., an opening parenthesis followed immediately by a closing parenthesis), or are the other bracket types also allowed to be deleted as matching pairs such as "[]", "<>", and "{}"?
If multiple occurrences of the substring "()" exist simultaneously, may we delete any one of them arbitrarily, or is there a required order (e.g., leftmost first)?
When a deletion occurs in the middle of the string, after concatenating the remaining parts, can newly formed adjacent characters create a new "()" substring that can be deleted in subsequent steps?
Are empty strings considered valid colorful bracket sequences, and should we output "Yes" for an input S that is already empty (if such a case were allowed by the constraints)?
Is the output case-sensitive, i.e., must we print exactly "Yes" and "No" with capital Y/N and lowercase rest, or are other capitalizations acceptable?

Are there any restrictions on the total number of deletion operations allowed (e.g., must the process terminate in at most |S| steps), or can we perform an arbitrary number of deletions as long as the string eventually becomes empty?

If the input string contains characters other than the six specified bracket types (due to malformed input), how should the program behave—should it treat the string as not colorful, or is such input guaranteed never to occur?

In the case where the string length is at the maximum limit (2 × 10⁵), are there any time or memory limits that affect the choice of algorithm, or is the standard competitive programming limit (e.g., 1‑2 seconds, 256 MB) assumed?

inline_prompts:
You are given a string S consisting of six types of characters.  
A string T is called a colorful bracket sequence if it satisfies the following condition:  
It is possible to turn T into an empty string by repeating the following operation any number of times (possibly zero):  
- If there exists a contiguous substring of T that is one of (), choose one such substring and delete it.  
- If the deleted substring was at the beginning or end of T, the remainder becomes the new T.  
- Otherwise, concatenate the part before the deleted substring and the part after the deleted substring, and that becomes the new T.  
Determine whether S is a colorful bracket sequence.  
Input  
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:  
S  
Output  
If S is a colorful bracket sequence, print Yes  
Constraints  
- S is a string of length between 1 and 2\times 10^5, inclusive.  
- S consists of (, ), [, ], <, >.
